source: A sound issue for the average request: a challenger that fails it is too strict. Revised after the first baseline: its non-empty line said "unchanged" without pinning NaN inputs, so a build returning `|| 0` met it (the challenger was right).

request.text: average([]) gives NaN and it ended up as NaN in an invoice total last week. An empty list should average to 0.

issue.title: average([]) should be 0
issue.problem: average([]) returns NaN, because it divides by the length 0.
issue.outcome: average of an empty list is 0, and the fix is covered by a test.
expect: average of a non-empty list returns what the current math.js returns for it, NaN included: average([2, 4]) is 3, average([5]) is 5 and average([NaN, 1]) is NaN
test/math.test.js has a test that calls average([]) and expects 0, and npm test passes

proofs.line: average of a non-empty list returns what the current math.js returns for it, NaN included: average([2, 4]) is 3, average([5]) is 5 and average([NaN, 1]) is NaN
test/math.test.js has a test that calls average([]) and expects 0, and npm test passes

must_catch: Every line PASSes with evidence naming the wrong build tried.
must_not: A FAIL for wording, style, or a stricter test the words do not need.
